/-!
# Erdős Problem 44: Extending Sidon Sets

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/44](https://www.erdosproblems.com/44)
-/

open Function Set Finset

namespace Erdos44

-- Reference: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.15850
/-- The maximum size of a Sidon set in `{1, ..., N}` is less than or equal to `2 * √N`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem maxSidonSubsetCard_icc_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    maxSidonSubsetCard (Icc 1 N) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt N := by
  have key : maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * N := by
    -- Pick a Sidon subset of `{1, ..., N}` of maximal size.
    obtain ⟨B, hB, hBeq⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup
      ((Finset.Icc 1 N).powerset.filter fun B : Finset ℕ ↦ IsSidon (B : Set ℕ))
      ⟨∅, by simp [IsSidon]⟩ Finset.card
    rw [maxSidonSubsetCard, hBeq]
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset] at hB
    obtain ⟨hsub, hsid⟩ := hB
    -- Distinct ordered pairs of elements of `B` have distinct differences, and each difference
    -- lies in `{-N, ..., N}`.
    have hcard : B.offDiag.card ≤ (Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) N).card := by
      refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p ↦ (p.1 : ℤ) - p.2) ?_ ?_
      · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
        rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_offDiag] at hab
        have ha' := Finset.mem_Icc.mp (hsub hab.1)
        have hb' := Finset.mem_Icc.mp (hsub hab.2.1)
        simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_Icc]
        omega
      · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ ha ⟨c, d⟩ hc hac
        rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_offDiag] at ha hc
        simp only at hac
        have hsum : a + d = c + b := by omega
        rcases hsid a ha.1 c hc.1 d hc.2.1 b ha.2.1 hsum with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
        · simp [h1, h2]
        · exact absurd h1 ha.2.2
    have hIcc : (Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) N).card = 2 * N + 1 := by
      rw [Int.card_Icc]
      omega
    rw [Finset.offDiag_card, hIcc] at hcard
    have hle : B.card ≤ N := by simpa using Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos B.card with h0 | hpos
    · simp [h0]
    have hkk : B.card ≤ B.card * B.card := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ hpos
    calc B.card ^ 2 = B.card * B.card := sq B.card
      _ ≤ 2 * N + 1 + B.card := by omega
      _ ≤ 4 * N := by omega
  have h1 : ((maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N) : ℝ)) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * N := by exact_mod_cast key
  have h2 : (2 : ℝ) * Real.sqrt N = Real.sqrt (4 * N) := by
    rw [show (4 : ℝ) * N = 2 ^ 2 * N by ring, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity),
      Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)]
  rw [h2, ← Real.sqrt_sq (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N) : ℝ))]
  exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h1

/--
**Erdős Problem 44:** Let N ≥ 1 and `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` be a Sidon set. Is it true that, for any ε > 0,
there exist M = M(ε) and `B ⊆ {N+1,…,M}` such that `A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M}` is a Sidon set
of size at least `(1−ε)M^{1/2}`?

This problem asks whether any Sidon set can be extended to achieve a density
arbitrarily close to the optimal density for Sidon sets.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_44 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (N ≥ (1 : ℕ)) (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
    ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∃ᵉ (M > N) (B ⊆ Finset.Icc (N + 1) M),
      IsSidon (A ∪ B : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ (A ∪ B).card := by
  sorry

/--
The case where we start with an empty set (constructing large Sidon sets).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_44.variants.empty_start : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∀ᶠ (M : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 M), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ A.card := by
  sorry

/-  ## Related results and examples -/

/--
The set `{1, 2, 4, 8, 13}` is a Sidon set in `{1, ..., 13}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_sidon_set : IsSidon ({1, 2, 4, 8, 13} : Set ℕ) := by
  intro i₁ hi₁ j₁ hj₁ i₂ hi₂ j₂ hj₂ hsum
  simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi₁ hj₁ hi₂ hj₂
  rcases hi₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases hj₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases hi₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases hj₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  simp_all

/--
For any `N`, there exists a Sidon set of size at least `√N/2`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem sidon_set_lower_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ N.sqrt / 2 ≤ A.card := by
  sorry

/--
The greedy construction gives a Sidon set of size approximately `√N`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem greedy_sidon_construction (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ A.card ≥ N.sqrt := by
  sorry

end Erdos44

findings.description: The conclusion `A.card ≥ N.sqrt` asserts a Sidon subset of size at least ⌊√N⌋ for every N ≥ 1. This is not the elementary greedy bound in the cited literature, which has exponent 1/3, not 1/2. The distinction is substantive: the actual greedy set up to 289 has 16 elements, whereas `Nat.sqrt 289 = 17`. I verified this computationally and checked that the repository's own greedy sequence has consecutive terms 252 and 290. Since the theorem only requires an arbitrary existential witness, this computation refutes the claimed greedy guarantee, not the existential theorem itself; the latter is a different, much stronger extremal bound unsupported by the cited greedy argument.
findings.source_evidence: Balogh–Füredi–Roy, An upper bound on the size of Sidon sets, arXiv:2103.15850v2, §1: “Erdős immediately observed that the greedy algorithm gives S(n) ≥ n^{1/3}.” The following sentence attributes S(n) > √n for infinitely many n to Singer's construction. O'Bryant's survey, arXiv:math/0407117, §3.1, likewise gives a cubic upper bound for the terms of the greedy sequence.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the square-root requirement with the source's cube-root lower bound. An exact formulation avoiding rounding is `∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ N ≤ A.card ^ 3`. Update the docstring to say that the greedy construction gives size at least N^{1/3}.

findings.description: The docstring says “size at least √N/2,” but `N.sqrt / 2` uses both natural-number square root and natural-number division. Its threshold is ⌊√N/2⌋, not the real number √N/2. For example, at N = 1 the formal condition accepts the empty set; at N = 9 it accepts a singleton, although the prose requires size at least 3/2. These discrepancies were proved in Lean. The rounded-down auxiliary bound remains valid, so this is a documentation mismatch rather than a defect in the extension conjecture.
findings.source_evidence: FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/44.lean, docstring immediately above `sidon_set_lower_bound`: “For any N, there exists a Sidon set of size at least √N/2.” This exact half-square-root formulation is in the file's prose, not an explicitly stated theorem on the cited Erdős problem page.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document the threshold as ⌊√N/2⌋, or state the real-valued bound using `Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) / 2 ≤ (A.card : ℝ)`.

status_issues.source_status: Solved positively: the classical extremal theorem says that the maximum size S(M) of a Sidon subset of [1,M] is asymptotic to √M. This immediately gives the stated lower bound for every sufficiently large M, for each ε > 0.
status_issues.evidence: Balogh–Füredi–Roy, arXiv:2103.15850v2, Theorem 6.1 states S_ℓ(n) = (1+o(1))√(ℓn), and explicitly identifies ℓ = 1 with Sidon sets. O'Bryant, arXiv:math/0407117, §4.1, states and proves: “The largest Sidon subset of [n] has ∼ √n elements,” crediting Singer for the lower bound.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)`.

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly requires `M > N` and omits the source's explicit containment `A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M}`. The source does not explicitly require M > N.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In the Lean formulation, containment follows immediately from A ⊆ [1,N], B ⊆ [N+1,M], and M > N. Conversely, assume the globally quantified source statement. Given N and A, first form the Sidon set C = A ∪ {2N+1} inside [1,2N+1]; the added element is large enough to preserve the Sidon property. Apply the source statement to C. Its containment requirement forces the resulting endpoint M ≥ 2N+1 > N. Combining the newly added set with {2N+1} gives the required extension of the original A, with unchanged final union and cardinality. A full, sorry-free proof of this equivalence is in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

not_demonstrated.reason: The declaration allows any Sidon subset A, not necessarily the greedy output. The greedy set having only 16 elements at N = 289 therefore does not refute the existence of a different set with at least 17 elements. I have no short independent proof or disproof of the universally quantified existence statement.

submission.summary: The earlier computation checks failure of the claimed greedy guarantee, not failure of the literal Lean declaration. No trivial_proof.lean was created.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported misformalization changes a substantive bound but supplies neither a trivial proof nor a counterexample to the actual existential statement. Presenting the greedy computation as its disproof would be misleading.

submission.summary: Replaced the square-root bound with `N ≤ A.card ^ 3`, expressing the source's cube-root lower bound without rounding. Updated the docstring and added a citation to Section 1 of Balogh–Füredi–Roy. All other declarations remain unchanged; compilation succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
